files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Added
- **Runway: how long your money will last.** Six new dashboard tiles (off by default, under Forecasting) show the date your money runs out and the months left, both at your current spending and if you stick to your budgets, with the difference between the two and a chart of the total running down to zero. You choose which accounts count, and the average is taken over the last 1 to 12 full months, 3 by default. Known one-off amounts in the future, in or out, can be added as planned one-offs and are applied on their dates. A spend you have ticked **Exclude from forecast** on is kept out of the average, so a one-time purchase doesn't make the figure look worse than it is. Budget can also send you a notification when the run-out date moves a month or more earlier. This comes with the runway tiles, it is only checked once you have added one or chosen accounts for the runway, and it is checked once a month so the usual ups and downs of a month don't set it off. It can be switched off with **Runway alerts** in the notification settings. The same figures are available from the API at `GET /api/v1/runway`. The runway tile replaces the Burn Rate tile, which never showed a figure, so if you had that on your dashboard it will be gone. A credit card balance is already part of the total, so don't add paying it off as a one-off.
- **Enable Banking for bank sync.** Enable Banking is now a bank-sync provider next to GoCardless and SimpleFIN, and unlike GoCardless it can be used for your own accounts privately. You create an application in the Enable Banking control panel, enter its ID and private key once in Budget (they are stored encrypted and kept out of backups), and connect your banks from **Bank Sync**. The bank sends you back to `/apps/budget/bank-sync/callback`, which is the redirect URL to register for the application. A normal sync only reads the accounts you have mapped, to stay inside the banks' daily limits. Contributed by @saesch83 ([#454](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/pull/454))
- **Dashboard charts and reports can count budget periods.** With a **Budget Cycle Start Day** set, Settings has **Months in dashboard charts and reports**, with **Calendar months** (the default) or **Budget periods**. With budget periods and start day 26, a salary on 26 September counts towards October in the dashboard's trend and spending charts, the summary trend, cash flow by month and the category × month report, the same as on the Budget page. The report presets then cover whole budget periods, and a line under each chart names the start day. Exports and scheduled reports of those reports follow the choice; year-over-year and the digest stay on calendar months. Reported by @saesch83 ([#457](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/457))
- **Bills no longer have to set budgets.** A category with no budget of its own takes the monthly total of its recurring bills and income as its budget, marked **auto** on the Budget page. **Budget categories from their bills** in Settings turns that off, so a category only has a budget when you set one. A parent you budget yourself then isn't topped up by its children's bills, setting a budget to 0 leaves the category with no budget, and a yearly bill no longer becomes a twelfth of itself every month. Bills, their reminders and payments work the same either way, and their spending still counts towards the parent's budget. It is on by default, so nothing changes until you switch it off. Requested by @EtienneLavanant ([#479](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/479))
- **Macedonian denar (MKD).** MKD can now be picked as an account or default currency, shown as ден after the amount, with a daily exchange rate like the other currencies. Reported by @vlatkojordanov90 ([#476](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/476))
- **The transactions CSV export names the attached receipts.** A **Receipts** column at the end of the export lists the file names of each transaction's receipts, separated by "; " if there are several, so an auditor can find the right invoice. The existing columns stay where they were. The names are the ones the files had when they were attached, and the column stays blank in an account someone has shared with you, as the receipts are the owner's. Reported by @malle214 ([#475](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/475))
- **Find Duplicates pairs a bill's payment with the bank's row of it.** A payment a bill booked (by auto-pay or Mark Paid) and the bank's own row of the same payment have different dates and text, so the duplicate finder never put them together. It now lists them in a section of their own when the bank row is the same amount to the penny, a few days away and names the bill, with a **Merge** button. Merge keeps the bank row, with its date, text and cleared status, gives it the bill, its category, tags and splits, and deletes the booked payment. A bill still waiting for its payment is paid with the bank row instead.
- **The import preview shows which rows pay a bill.** Step 3 of the import has a **Matched to bills** count and a **Bill** badge on each matching row, and says how many rows could be the payment of more than one bill. Those rows are imported without a bill, to be matched from Find Duplicates or with **Link to bill**, rather than guessed at.
- **Bill payments the bank hasn't shown are listed on the Bills page.** In an account that takes statements or bank sync, a bill more than a week overdue with no payment found, and an auto-paid payment no bank row has turned up for in a week, are listed with **Mark Paid**, **Skip** and **Edit bill**, or **It went out** for an auto-paid one.
- **Budgets can be shown in the Bills Calendar.** A new calendar button on each expense budget on the Budget page puts that budget in **Reports > Bills Calendar** as estimated spending: its own row, marked Budget, with the month's share of the budget in every month, counted in the monthly totals, the chart, the CSV and PDF exports, and the bills calendar feed as an event on the 1st of each month. **Include budgeted spending** in the report turns them off again. Only a budget amount you set counts, so a category's bills are never counted twice, and budgets are left out when one account is picked, as a budget has no account. Requested by @TerjeTM ([#459](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/459))
- **Promotional rates on credit cards and loans.** Credit cards, loans, mortgages and lines of credit have a **Promotional rate** group in the account form, with the rate (usually 0), the date it starts (today unless you change it) and the date it ends, and **Remove promotional rate** to take it off again. Until the end date the Debt Payoff plan charges the promotional rate and then the normal one, avalanche ranks your debts again each month by the rate in effect, and when the promotion ends the plan raises that debt's minimum if it no longer covers the interest. Accrued interest uses the promotional rate for the days inside the window without touching the rate history, so nothing needs changing when it ends. Budget sends a Nextcloud notification to the account owner 30 days before the end date, once, and again if you change the date. The account page shows "0% until 12 Mar 2027", or "ended" afterwards. If you already added a 0% entry to the rate history by hand for a promotion, delete it after setting the promotional rate, or interest stays at 0% after the end date.
- **Budget Breakdown tile settings.** The Budget Breakdown tile now has the same settings as Budget Progress: the date range (including the current budget period, which stays the default), one account or all of them, leaving out accounts shared with you, and top-level categories only. Requested by @TerjeTM ([#480](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/480))

### Changed
- **Translations.** German is now fully translated, and French has a few new strings, from the translators on Weblate.

### Fixed
- **Imports match the bank's rows to bills with no auto-detect pattern.** A bill with no pattern was passed by on import, so the bank's row of a payment auto-pay or Mark Paid had already booked went in beside it and the money left the account twice, and a bill still waiting for its payment stayed overdue. Such a bill is now matched by its name: the bank row has to be in the bill's account, the same amount to the penny, within 5 days of the payment (**Settings > Import & Export > Bill match window**), and name the bill, so "Claude.ai" matches "ANTHROPIC* CLAUDE" and "Ee" matches "EE LIMITED" but not "COFFEE". The bank row then takes the booked payment's place, or pays the bill. A row that could be more than one payment is left for you. Bills with a pattern match as before.
- **Auto-pay books a payment as pending until the bank shows it.** In an account that takes statements or bank sync, auto-pay now books its payment as pending rather than cleared, still counted in the balance, and the bank's row replaces it as cleared when it comes in. An account you keep by hand still gets a cleared payment.
- **Reconciliation can be finished when everything is already reconciled.** The starting balance left out transactions already marked reconciled, either dated after the statement date on a first reconciliation or reconciled outside a reconciliation since the last one, and those can't be ticked, so the difference never reached zero and **Finish** stayed greyed out. The starting balance now includes them, and **Create adjustment** is offered when there is nothing left to tick. A reconciliation that is already stuck keeps its old starting balance, so cancel it and start again. Reported by @filug ([#473](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/473))
- **Trend charts keep their last month.** The income vs. expenses trend stepped a month at a time from the start date, so a range like 26 July to 25 October lost October, and a range starting on 31 January skipped February. It now lists every month the range touches, in calendar mode too.
- **The dashboard's "% vs last month" compares like with like.** The income, expenses and cash flow tiles read the current period's calendar-month buckets, so with a start day the comparison was missing or compared two halves of one period. They now compare this budget period so far with the same number of days of the one before, up to and including its last day, so the 1st of the month no longer reads "down 100%" and 28 February is compared with 28 days of January, not all 31. Last-day fix contributed by @saesch83 ([#478](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/pull/478))
- **Receipt scanning reads the date the right way round.** A date printed as 08/11/2026 could come back as 11 August on a receipt in pounds, as the model picked the day and month order itself. Budget now asks for the date as printed and works out the order from the receipt's currency, or your default currency when the receipt doesn't show one, so it is 8 November in pounds or euros and 11 August in dollars. A date that could be either and gives no clue (a receipt in Canadian dollars) is left blank for you to fill in.
- **Bank sync shows what the bank sends as text.** The balance and currency in **Account Mappings** went into the page as they came from the bank provider, so a provider sending markup could run script in Budget. They are now shown as plain text, and the server only keeps a currency that is a three-letter code and a balance that is a number.
- **The bank authorization page opens safely.** The GoCardless authorization link now opens with no link back to the Budget window and no referrer, and the server refuses a link that isn't https before your browser sees it. The "click here to authorize" link is always shown, since the browser can no longer say whether the window opened.
- **A factory reset ends your bank connections at the provider.** Factory reset, clearing the sample data and purging a deleted user removed the bank connections from Budget but left the consent at GoCardless or Enable Banking running, as only **Disconnect** revoked it. They now revoke each connection once the data has gone. A provider that can't be reached is logged and never stops the reset.
- **Dashboard tiles scroll when their content doesn't fit.** Budget Breakdown, Top Spending Categories, Large Transactions and a dozen more of the optional tiles cut off whatever didn't fit, so a long budget list or a wide table lost its last rows and columns. They now scroll inside the tile, the same as Recent Transactions and Upcoming Bills. Reported by @TerjeTM ([#480](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/480))
- **Budget Progress keeps the budget period when you pick an account.** The tile shows the current budget period until you choose a range, but its settings showed **Last 6 months**, and choosing only an account switched the tile to 6 months. The settings now show **Current budget period**, and picking an account keeps it.
- **Bank sync errors no longer put credentials in the log.** A failed connect, sync or bank list logged the error with its stack trace, and on PHP 8.1 that trace can hold the decrypted bank credentials. These errors are now logged with their type and message only. The message you see is the same as before.
